name: prime

relevance.justification: PRIME contains 53,449 human 16S rRNA amplicon samples from 111 public studies with species-level microbial abundance (phylum through species via SILVA 138.2 and Greengenes2 2024.09), 101 phenotypic categories (including disease status), and per-sample host metadata including age, sex, and BMI. Ethnicity/race is not explicitly confirmed in the paper schema. Data is fully structured (CSV). Actively maintained (Zenodo deposit June 2025, paper published January 2026). NCBI taxon IDs used for taxon mapping.

novelty.justification: No existing BioThings API covers human 16S rRNA microbiome abundance data at per-sample resolution with linked host demographics and phenotypes. GMrepo covers gut microbiome but is restricted to gut/fecal samples; PRIME covers 93 body sites across 10 body systems. The entity type (microbiome sample with per-taxon read counts and relative abundances linked to host demographics) is entirely new to BioThings. 53,449 samples from 111 studies provide novel breadth.

openness.justification: All files freely downloadable from Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.15711237) without login, account, or API key. Dual-licensed CC-BY 4.0 + MIT. No click-through gate. Attribution required under CC-BY 4.0 but no commercial restriction. PRIME homepage states data is 'openly accessible without login or restriction'.

evidence.scope: Human-associated 16S rRNA amplicon microbiome data. Contains: (1) taxonomic abundance tables (absolute read counts + relative abundances) at phylum/class/order/family/genus/species for SILVA 138.2 and Greengenes2 2024.09 reference databases; (2) per-sample metadata including body site (93 sites across 10 systems), phenotypic category (101 categories), age, sex, BMI, disease status, sequencing protocol, and data quality scores; (3) per-study metadata for 111 source studies.
evidence.overlap: Partial overlap with GMrepo (gut/fecal microbiome, also 16S). No overlap with MyChem, MyGene, MyDisease, or MyVariant. PRIME substantially extends GMrepo: 93 body sites vs gut-only, 53,449 samples vs GMrepo's scope, 101 phenotype categories vs GMrepo's disease focus, and DADA2-reprocessed standardized abundance values vs study-native formats.

api_info.record_coverage: query access; custom subset download via async generation (available within 24h)

risks: Ethnicity/race field not explicitly confirmed in samples_metadata.csv schema — verify during site inspection
Bulk abundance files are large (up to 1.8 GB per file; 9.1 GB total) — ingestion strategy must handle file size
Controlled phenotype vocabulary is PRIME-internal (not MONDO/HPO) — entity resolution to standard ontologies needed
Body site categorization uses PRIME's own 10-system hierarchy — mapping to standard ontology (UBERON/FMA) needed
Custom subset downloads via async generation are not suitable for bulk ingestion — use Zenodo static files instead
NCBI taxon ID mapping described as attempted but may be incomplete for all annotated taxa
next_actions: Run site inspection to verify Zenodo file access, confirm samples_metadata.csv column schema, and check API endpoints
Determine ingestion strategy: species-level abundance tables (SILVA or GG2 or both) + samples_metadata.csv as primary files
Resolve phenotype controlled vocabulary to MONDO/HPO CURIEs
Map body site hierarchy to UBERON CURIEs
Confirm ethnicity/race field presence in metadata
